name: Executive order of March 29, 1884 restoring most of the Turtle Mountain Reservation to the public domain
aka: amended by executive order of June 3, 1884
citation: Executive Order of March 29, 1884, amended by Executive Order of June 3, 1884
nations: Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians
promises: The executive order of December 21, 1882 had set apart a reserve for the band, which the State Historical Society of North Dakota puts at 20 townships.
today: Royce records that the order restored the 1882 reserve to the public domain except Townships 162 and 163 North, Range 71 West, kept for the band; the June 3, 1884 order swapped in Township 162 North, Range 70 West. The State Historical Society of North Dakota says the two townships left were not large enough for the tribe. The Court of Claims held in 1974 that the executive orders of December 21, 1882 and March 29, 1884 did not extinguish Chippewa aboriginal title, since nothing showed Congress authorized it or that the Chippewas accepted the reservation as a settlement of their claims. The Indian Claims Commission then valued 8,104,040 acres as taken on February 15, 1905 under the McCumber Agreement of October 22, 1892, as amended by the Act of April 21, 1904 (33 Stat. 189, 193), at $53,527,225.00 against $999,887.03 paid, held that consideration unconscionable, and found the plaintiffs entitled to $52,527,337.97 less offsets (September 20, 1978). That finding concerns the 1904 to 1905 taking, a separate record.

openQuestions: What was found about this order: in 1974 the Court of Claims rejected the government's argument that it (with the 1882 order) extinguished the band's title. No court or Commission held this order itself to be a taking or a breach; the compensated taking is dated February 15, 1905. Under the project rule an executive-order reduction alone is not a breach, so this stays 'no breach found yet'.
Whether the 20 townships restored in 1884 lie inside the 8,104,040 acres the Commission valued was not confirmed against its maps.
The Turtle Mountain Band's own website (tmbci.org) did not load, so the nation's account is missing.
